claims.statement: Elastic documents a Personal/User Elasticsearch API key type that lets external services access the Elasticsearch and Kibana APIs on behalf of a user.

sources.supports: Personal/User API key: allows external services to access the Elastic Stack, including the Elasticsearch and Kibana APIs, on behalf of a user.

claims.statement: The create-API-key response carries the key as separate id and api_key fields and, since Elasticsearch 7.16.0 and on Serverless, an encoded field defined as the base64 encoding of the UTF-8 representation of id and api_key joined by a colon.

sources.supports: API key credentials which is the base64-encoding of the UTF-8 representation of `id` and `api_key` joined by a colon (`:`).
sources.locator: class Response, fields id, api_key, encoded

claims.statement: Elastic documents the encoded API key value as the credential sent in the Authorization header with the ApiKey scheme.

sources.supports: You must create an API key and use the encoded value in the request header: Authorization: ApiKey ${API_KEY}

openQuestions.question: Which base64 alphabet and padding the encoded field uses, and the length and alphabet of the generated api_key and id values, are not stated in the pages read; the family is not researched beyond existence and the documented encoded representation.
Whether the id half of the pair is documented as non-secret on its own is not established by the pages read; it must not be treated as a benign sibling until a source says so.
This candidate is recorded from the claims above only; format, variants, history and benign siblings have not been researched.
